newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Future children may wear "smart" shoes, pants.
newsitem.headline: Future children may wear "smart" shoes, pants.

text.p: Children of the future may carry information in their shoes instead of their heads and wear "smarty pants" which regulate their classroom temperature, a European politician predicted on Monday.

"Futuristic technologies (are) the stuff of science fact not of science fiction," Eluned Morgan, a British member of the European Parliament, told a news conference to launch her report on education, culture and the information society.

There were prototypes of computer-bearing shoes into which children could download whole books and "wearable" memory computers which recorded everything a person sees and hears in a lifetime, she said.
Morgan said developments in computer technology and the Internet offered marvellous opportunities for children and adults to have almost instant access to information on every subject under the sun.
She admitted not every parent could afford new smart shoes -- especially when their offspring outgrow them every two months or persist in wearing them to play football on the way home.
